images.name: cover
images.title: An *AI Administrative Assistant* runs the office admin
images.sub: The shared inbox, bookings, forms, filing, orders and reports: what it owns, what stays with a person, and what the job costs.

images.name: duties
images.title: The admin job, *duty by duty*
rows: Reads and files every email and voicemail, answers routine questions from written answers and forwards the rest with a summary.
Books meetings across calendars, reserves rooms, sends reminders and rebooks cancellations.
Enters intake forms, delivery notes and documents into the right system and flags anything that doesn't match.
Files documents by the office's rules and chases renewals 30 days before insurance or licences lapse.
Places routine reorders under a set limit. Larger or new-supplier orders are prepared and held.
Sends the Friday reports and follows up on missing forms and quotes.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A day at a *property management company*
rows: Sorts 63 weekend emails. Logs 11 maintenance requests in the work order system.
Two tenants booked the amenity room for Saturday. Offers the second one Sunday, and they accept.
Sends the owner the vacancy report, built from the leasing system.
A plumbing contractor's insurance lapsed Friday. Requests the new certificate.
A vendor emails asking to change their bank details. Held for a phone check.
A $2,400 furniture quote for the leasing office. Prepared and held for approval.
Reorders printer paper and cleaning supplies under the limit and files the day's documents.

images.name: setup
images.title: Setting up an *AI Administrative Assistant*
steps: Every task, where the information came from, where it went and how long it took.
Routine answers, filing rules, spending limits and what always goes to a person.
Shared inbox, calendar, document storage and the business software, with only the access the job needs.
It prepares replies, bookings and entries, and a person approves them for the first couple of weeks.
Hand over one duty at a time
Inbox and filing first, then bookings, then data entry. Money comes last.
Someone reads the log and updates the rules when a supplier, form or system changes.
